messages.author: 9ba770a788c3d1b6
messages.subject: [GSoC student proposal]  Reproducible working and developing environment for R (Rbundler)
parts:
I know it's very late to bring a new proposal, but I just got the idea. The idea is simple, and the benefit shall be clear, for anyone who had ever struggled to resolve the broken dependences of some old code or code from other persons. Meanwhile, I'm contacting some experienced R developers in person, so hopefully, I can find some mentors in time. The details of proposal is following,

Summary: Reproducible working and developing environment for R (Rbundler)

Student: Chenliang Xu

Description: R handles dependences of packages properly and automatically, so we only need to call a few commands to installed all the required packages for a project. However, it’s quite often the dependences become broken after half year or so, because new versions of R and/or packages bring some conflicts. Furthermore, the claim “packages A, B, C must be installed” might actually mean “packages A, B, C  and some other packages on my current computer must be installed”. Without a clean prescription, it’s hard to reproduce the required working environment, not to mention the reproducible research result.

Inspired by Ruby/bundler, I would like to propose a method for reproducing working and developing environment for R reliably. By specifying the required packages and R version in a file in the project directory, a single call to command `Rbundler install` shall grab all the required packages, save them in cache and install them in local lib directory. It shall also create a snapshot file to describe the version of packages used. With the snapshot file and cached packages, the command `Rbundler restore snapshot_name` shall rebuild the same working environment exactly, on the same machine in the future or any other machines.

Target: A cross platform (Linux, Mac and Windows with proper developing tools installed) tool Rbundler supporting the following command,

  • Rbundler install  Download and cache the required packages, install them in local lib directory.

  • Rbundler restore snapshot_name Restore specific status of working environment on any computer.

  • Rbundler run Run R with local lib directory added to lib path.

  • Rbundler run --clean Run R in a clean environment, with only local lib directory in lib path.

Skills required: It’s more about the procedure of building, installing and loading R packages, rather than R programming.

Possible Side projects:  This section shows some potential benefits of this project. I may pursue them in the future, but they are not part of the Google summer of code project.

  • If the binary packages can be cached properly, we can prepare a clean environment with all the required dependencies, for testing and building R package easily and quickly.

  • Combining the lightweight Linux container docker and Rbundler, we may easily deploy the production environment, including the external dependencies, to a Linux server or cloud.

messages.subject: Re: [GSoC student proposal] Reproducible working and developing environment for R (Rbundler)
parts:
Hi Chenliang,

There's an existing project called "packrat" that is also inspired directly by Bundler: http://rstudio.github.io/packrat/

If that's close enough to what you are looking for then perhaps the Docker work that you outlined might be an interesting extension?

J.J.

messages.author: 9ba770a788c3d1b6
messages.subject: Re: [GSoC student proposal] Reproducible working and developing environment for R (Rbundler)
parts:
Oops...I should knew that package earlier. It's exactly the same as my proposal. For the Docker, I was able to reproduce the book Reproducible Research with R/RStudio from its source code on github. The book uses lots of packages and also absolute path, so it's not as easy as looks like. With the help of docker, I was able to get a clear prescription for reproducing the book. However, I'm not convinced on the usefulness of Docker for R developing, except for the special case. Most of R packages don't have any external dependencies, and packrat::restore should resolve the dependencies for most of R project.

Thanks!


Best,
Chenliang Xu
